rationale: Greek loanword αἰτητής 'one who demands.' In the body-as-storehouse parable of this kephalaion, the αἰτητής is the appetitive principle (Hyle's voice through the archon) which perpetually demands tribute from the senses' storehouses. Standard agentive form, fits the legal-fiscal register of demand/payment governing the body.
Verbal root underlying ⲡⲁⲓⲧⲏⲧⲏⲥ above; in line 29 ⲉⲧⲱⲓⲧⲉ 'who claims/demands.' Possibly Lyc. reflex of ⲱⲧⲉ 'press, urge.' Confidence moderate.

Possessive ⲡⲉϩ- 'his' + ⲧⲁⲱ. Already in accumulated vocabulary as ⲛⲧⲁⲱ 'of boundary' (in eschatological bōlos context). Here, in agricultural-genealogical context 'each one in his ⲡⲉϩⲧⲁⲱ,' the sense is 'his appointed kind / his measure / his bounded portion.' The boundary-semantics fit: each begotten one is delimited to his own kind.
Line 31. Possibly Lyc. variant of ⲡⲱⲧ 'run, flee, course.' In the context of enthumesis 'going outside, running after [something]' the verb of motion-pursuit fits. Confidence low.

proposed_english: to match them / to correspond them
rationale: Line 27. Future relative form ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲛⲁⲱⲛⲧⲟⲩ. Possibly from ⲟⲩⲱⲛⲧ 'compare, equate' with 3pl object. The correspondential register of the storehouse-passage supports a verb of correspondence-establishment (interior storehouse matches external object). Alternative readings include ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲡ 'transfer.' Confidence low.
